rationale: Evidence: iteration 9 (kp 2.5, kd 1.2, ki 0, base 1.2, 16 mm sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, mass 0.6 kg, body 0.14 m, wheel track 0.14 m) is the best design so far at 917.47. Its oval finishes 20/20 at 2.12 s, its s-bend finishes 20/20 at 2.35 s, and its slalom finishes 17/20 with 0.15 line-loss events per run. Iteration 10 raised kp to 2.75 and scored lower (902.2), with slalom finishes falling back to 16/20 and line-loss events rising to 0.35. So kp has passed its useful point, and kp 2.5 sits at the peak of the kp sweep. Iteration 8 showed kd is saturated (kd 1.5 gave no gain), and iteration 7 showed kp 2.0 loses too much turn authority. Decision: this is the final iteration and the final score is on an unseen track of different shape, so I am resubmitting the proven iteration 9 design unchanged rather than testing a new variable. Geometry and gains are identical to iteration 9. Expected result: about 915 to 920 on the development tracks, with the slalom at 0.85 finishes or better. Hypotheses: (H1) the slalom residual failures are a turn-authority limit that kp 2.5 already mostly covers; (H2) the unseen track will show similar oval and s-bend performance, with its tightest bend deciding the outcome. Measurements wanted per track: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort and noise_robustness, so the failure mode on any unseen track can be separated into line loss or overshoot.
